svg.title: Why a flat phone sleeve is wider than the phone
svg.desc: A cross-section of a phone inside a flat sleeve. The fabric has to go all the way around the phone: 2 times (3.07 plus 0.34) is 6.82 inches. Folded flat, each face of the sleeve is half of that, 3.41 inches, before seams and ease. Adding about a stitch for the side seams and a little ease gives about 3.9 inches, or 16 single crochet at 4 per inch. A sleeve chained to the phone's 3.07 inch width is too narrow.
svg.text: Looking down into the sleeve, phone inside
Fabric all the way round: 2 x (3.07 + 0.34) = 6.82 in
Each flat face is half of that: 3.41 in, before seams
Plus seams and a little ease: about 3.9 in
At 4 sc per inch: 16 sc wide, not 13.
Chained to 3.07 in, the inside is about 3.0 in. The phone
needs 3.41 in because the fabric also covers its edges.
